intent: My partner surprised me with a secondhand espresso machine, and now the bean decision is stalling me at the shelf. Fancy single-origin arabica bags cost more than double the supermarket espresso blends, and opinions on robusta swing between crema magic and burnt-rubber garbage. I pull two shots a day, almost always with milk, so this sets a real monthly bill. Is there actual chemistry behind the arabica-robusta split and the price gap, or does steamed milk flatten most of it anyway? What did people who agonized over this eventually settle into rebuying? Finish with the bag you'd put on my counter.

intent_v1_legacy: My kid was just diagnosed with type 1 and reading about how far treatment has come is oddly comforting. Can you walk me through the whole story, from insulin being discovered back in the 1920s, through the first pills, then pumps, up to these artificial-pancreas systems and the personalized stuff now? I'd love to follow it era by era and understand what actually changed each time. A clear picture of how today's treatments are organized would help too, plus any old beliefs about diabetes the community now knows were flat wrong.
